articles.title: As Dream's search for first WNBA Finals win continues, Atlanta optimistic for Game 2 rebound: 'We were right there'
articles.summary: Reality hit the Atlanta Dream in their Finals Game 1 loss. How can they rebound for Game 2?
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The what-ifs will always haunt a coach.

If Rhyne Howard's 25-footer went down in a one-point game. If Naz Hillmon's attempt from two feet farther out didn't pop out of the basket.

Then Atlanta Dream head coach Karl Smesko might not be talking about whatever mistakes the Dream made, and would instead be talking about how they secured the franchise's first WNBA Finals victory in its 18-year history.

Then Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase would be the one sitting between her players, highlighting misses instead of makes and stars who came up empty instead of those ascending.

But reality hit the Atlanta Dream, who came into the Finals on a 10-game winning streak, including five straight in the postseason. In what is their fourth Finals appearance in franchise history, they remain winless after a 68-64 loss in Game 1 on Saturday at Chase Center.

It left Smesko to stare down the missed 3-pointers and analyze how the defense limited Angel Reese, while Nakase praised her leading scorer Gabby Williams as " one of the best players in the world. "

"We were right there. Right there," Smesko said. "So that's why it hurts a little bit, but it also motivates us. We know what we're capable of doing."

Game 1 of the WNBA Finals met the week-long expectations for a matchup of two elite defenses . It was messy, sluggish, long and physical. It was such a battle that, when asked about a collision that included Williams, Nakase had to ask which one.

What stuck closest to the expected script was that it came down to a single possession at the wire. The Valkyries were the ones to arguably steal the win despite playing at home by fighting back late, taking the lead with 1:18 to play and holding it down the stretch.

Williams said the Valks had the Dream "right where we wanted them" despite trailing in the final minutes. They led for a total of 6:08, all coming within the final three minutes of each quarter. Those are the moments the Dream need to erase moving forward with an offense that lacked the muster in Game 1.

"I thought our team defended for the whole game excellent," Smesko said. "But when a game is this close, even a couple breakdowns can make the difference."

In a series so heavily reliant on defenses, it shaped up to be a matchup won in the margins — and by the team that could maintain composure at the end. Atlanta came into Chase Center staking claim to the offensive advantage, averaging 91.3 points per game in the regular season (third). The Valkyries mingled at the other end, averaging 82.2 points per game (second to last).

Atlanta can turn to top-10 league scorer Allisha Gray, who returned from a hand injury that kept her out of the semifinals, or perimeter specialist Howard. Reese in the paint can erase a litany of sins, and her emerging 3-point shot increases the danger. DeWanna Bonner, their August signing, boosts their bench and spacing and is facing the Valkyries for the first time as a member of the Dream.

But their collective 64 points were the worst production of their season, beating the previous low of 68 against Golden State in June. The 82.1 offensive rating came close to a season-low, and marked the first time in the playoffs it dropped below 103. The Valkyries defense, historically the best compared to the record-setting offense it faced, got the best of them.

It didn't start that poorly. In a 22-14 first-quarter lead, Reese became the fifth player in WNBA history to score at least 11 points on 80% shooting or better (5 of 6) in the opening quarter of a WNBA Finals game.

Over the next three quarters, she went without a bucket (0 for 5), including no shot attempts in the third quarter. That lack of production she took on herself, versus crediting the Valkyries.

"I don't really think they did anything," Reese said. "Maybe that was just on me. I wasn't aggressive enough with the ball and trying to get the ball and get to my spots. So definitely going to do a better job of that next game."

The team described Reese last week as their engine. The third-year forward came into the matchup setting the postseason on fire in her first career appearance. She averaged 19.1 points, shooting 56.2% from the floor, with 3.7 assists and 2.3 steals over their 10-game winning streak. All eclipsed her season-long marks of 16.4 points (45.1%), 2.8 assists and 1.8 steals.

"Angel had a great first half," Smesko said. "We didn't get her the ball enough. Those will be some things that we talk about for Game 2."

The Game 1 performance was not her worst statistically of the postseason. She added 12 rebounds — tying a career postseason high — with 2 steals and 1 block. She also wasn't the only one in red as Howard finished 3 of 14 from the field (2 of 9 from 3-point range) and Gray was 5 of 19 (1 of 8 from 3). No one shooting at volume was efficient.

Reese also had four turnovers, tying a career postseason high, that contributed to the Valkyries' 17 points off of 12 Atlanta turnovers. And she committed five personal fouls for a third time in six games, including two pivotal ones in the final 1:18.

Her first on Williams flipped the game from a one-point lead to a one-point deficit. The second on Kiah Stokes came trailing by one again. It's those types of plays that will change a game between two equally matched teams.

Possessions are at a premium when each team is shooting worse than 33% from the field and barely breaking 20% from the perimeter. Their combined 32% was second-worst ever in a WNBA Finals game. The Valkyries attempted five fewer free throws, shot 68.8% from the stripe, and still won. They bested the Dream in paint points (32-30), rebounds (41-35), second-chance points (8-4) and didn't allow them to feast off backcourt steal-and-scores.

The post-game Dream scene laid bare the punch of a Finals-opening loss. The franchise is 0-10 in Finals games, a sharp realization following their win streak to get back here. But they aren't done yet. The Valkyries forced the Dream to play their style, and still nearly dropped the opener.

"We're just going to have to watch some film, make some adjustments and come out and compete again as hard as we possibly can," Smesko said. "Because we obviously want to leave here winning Game 2."

articles.title: NBA storylines to watch in 2026-27: Can the 76ers sacrifice? Is Victor Wembanyama unstoppable?
articles.summary: A summer full of signings, scrimmaging and scandal has laid the runway for what should be one of the most compelling campaigns in recent memory.
articles.body:
Welcome, friends. After what has seemed like the longest offseason in basketball history, the official start of the 2026-27 NBA season tips off Tuesday.

A summer full of signings, scrimmaging and scandal has laid the runway for what should be one of the most compelling campaigns in recent memory. Here are five things we'll be paying close attention to.

Assuming the new-look 76ers aren't on pace to break every standing NBA offensive record, someone (or multiple someones) will need to concede certain aspects of their game, contrary to what Joel Embiid boldly declared last week .

We're not going to pay too much attention to their 27th-ranked offense through four preseason games — a plethora of moving parts were at work here — but it's important to note some stylistic changes that should spill over to the regular season. Players like Embiid and Jaylen Brown, who have historically been focal points, have seen immediate changes in their usage rates (28.8 for Embiid, 26.2 for Brown) — particularly Brown, who is seeing almost 10% less of the ball than in his final season in Boston.

Incorporating LeBron, who I believe is still the most important piece of the equation, hasn't taken as long as I would have assumed. His whopping 42.9 assist rate this preseason is higher than at any point over the past five seasons, which isn't saying much because it's early October, but it's still clear he's trying to ingratiate himself, and the team is bending to his tendencies (Philly led the league in assist rate this preseason).

What we do have is an idea of how the 76ers will operate. They'll shoot a bunch of 3s and play at an uptempo pace to maximize how lethal James and Tyrese Maxey are in space. More focus will be put on transitional defense than on crashing the offensive glass, and expect a flurry of smart off-ball movement from the Philly 4 to account for their lack of elite individual shooting. The biggest "sacrifices" will need to come from Embiid and Brown. More screening angles, less stationary activity around the nail and blocks for Embiid, less stagnation from Brown. This experiment can work, but only with clear understanding across the board.

One of the joys about the flurry of offseason movement is when the excitement about new star duos becomes tangible. It's even more heartwarming seeing how these partnerships empower one another.

Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball are long-lost cousins, bringing new life to the Midwest. Paul George recently spoke about playing with Jayson Tatum and rediscovering a passion for playing that was lost previously. Social media recently captured a moment between Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo where the Heat center urged his new teammate to be more aggressive, taking shots he routinely does behind the scenes in practice.

But what does all of this look like X's and O's-wise once the real games start and within the context of their teams? How will the Wolves react to the potential staggering of Edwards and Ball from a defensive standpoint? Can George continue to showcase more of a role-playing spirit as he did toward the end of his 76ers tenure — and how does Boston's playmaking tree change alongside Derrick White and Payton Pritchard? In Miami, does Giannis adopt more of a lead playmaker role and does that affect Davion Mitchell's development and expectations? Is there another lever to pull when Miami's floor spacing caves in? What about up north in Toronto, where Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes stem from the same defensive tree — is there enough perimeter versatility to become more aggressive in passing lanes for the others? So many new partnerships, so many new questions.

Is Victor Wembanyama about to take another leap?

What do you do next as a 22-year-old generational talent, coming off the first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year award in NBA history and your first Finals trip? It's hard to imagine how much better Victor Wembanyama can get, but the Frenchman's humble-yet-confident nature, combined with head coach Mitch Johnson's creativity, could yield some tantalizing results.

Perhaps it's due to his sheer presence within a Spurs organization that built its reputation on shared playmaking responsibilities, but Wemby becoming a more involved (and capable) creator is exactly what San Antonio needs with their new three-guard setup . In the preseason, Wembanyama was often seen conducting traffic from the top of the key and the slot, allowing the likes of Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle to slash to the rim and affording the Spurs as much space as functionally possible. There's a clear focus to get him more centralized to San Antonio's half-court scheme, one that will improve his already impressive processor and intangibles.

Last season, Wembanyama's assist rate (17.0) and assist-to-turnover ratio (1.28) were positive and indicative of growth in a scaled-up role. His preseason figures jumped (24.5 and 1.71, respectively), and this is still without Tobias Harris, who is currently sidelined with a calf issue. Featuring Wemby at the beginning of sets as opposed to having him deploy as a finisher certainly puts more trust in the surrounding talent, but there's enough depth and versatility to raise the Spurs' floor and ceiling by some notches.

Fallout from the Kawhi-Clippers investigation

The story of the summer has been written, discussed and talked about ad nauseam, but how exactly the league plans on moving on from the Clippers' cap-circumvention scandal — and the potential trickle-down effects for other teams in their dealings — is fascinating.

Over the years, the NBA has tried to curb nefarious activity, from anti-tanking rules and new measures in place to how injuries are reported, free agency no-nos and everything in between. What hasn't been as much of a focus, at least until now, is how to effectively govern contracts.

Take Milwaukee's Gary Trent Jr., for example. The veteran wing was one of the league's bottom-40 performers last season while playing on a minimum contract. How he somehow parlayed that production into a new four-year, $64 million deal is a question only a league internal investigation can answer. But the issue isn't as much about why Trent got a payday in 2026 as it is about what went on in the previous years under the guise of smaller compensation. Did anything take place that shouldn't have?

Will every signing from this point onward be met with doubt and wonder? Are teams still willing to blur the lines between professional and personal if the outcome is adding star talent, boosting the local economy and increasing organizational valuation? It's such a murky lake to wade into, especially considering the Kawhi Leonard fallout, suspensions, fines, and, more importantly, morality and dignity.

Commissioner Adam Silver, the league office and the Board of Governors went to great lengths to curb the tanking epidemic, resulting in an expanded draft lottery, a new lottery ball setup and stricter pick rules. Will it work?

Under the new rules, teams are prohibited from selecting in the top five in three successive seasons. With these updated guidelines, teams like Utah (who selected fifth in 2025 and second in 2026) would be strongly discouraged from tanking, which is refreshing. The Jazz lost starting center Walker Kessler in free agency — and reserve Jusuf Nurkić is sidelined as well — but adding Jaren Jackson Jr. at the trade deadline last season and drafting Darryn Peterson with the No. 2 pick gives them a strong, competitive base to build on.

The general thought process here is that the more often teams show up in the draft lottery, the less they should want to return to the bottom. Let's exclude the Chicagos and Memphises of the world; we're not expecting them to suddenly flip the page and be viable franchises (although I'm much higher on the Grizzlies than the average person). But the Wizards (who had the No. 1 pick in 2026), Mavericks (No. 1 in 2025) and Hornets (No. 4, 2025) all seem to be building toward winning programs. Enough summer business has transpired within those organizations to suggest such, and diving back toward the bottom in some faint hope of landing on another top prospect — in a less-than-stellar 2027 crop — seems suboptimal.

Where it gets interesting is how the "3-2-1" rule now awards the eighth-placed team in each conference with a lottery ping-pong ball. Those teams would have a 2.7% chance at landing the top overall pick (as opposed to a zero-percent chance previously) — and could potentially alter how teams operate over the final few weeks of the regular season. Does a team sitting in sixth or seventh place, fully aware of its realistic contention chances, take a step back and try for lottery luck? This expansive approach from Silver, while bold and noble, could open up a whole different set of unknowns.

articles.title: LeBron Shared Nike's 'Dream' of Joining Knicks & 'Always Flirted with the Idea,' Reveal NBA Insiders
articles.summary: It's no secret that star forward LeBron James once considered joining the New York Knicks before ultimately signing with the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency this offseason, but it sounds like he wasn't alone with that idea.
articles.body:
It's no secret that star forward LeBron James once considered joining the New York Knicks before ultimately signing with the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency this offseason, but it sounds like he wasn't alone with that idea.

During Monday's episode of The Hoop Collective (5:15 mark), ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported that Nike had hoped to see James land with the Knicks before he even entered the NBA in 2003.

"There was this dream, and it was kind of LeBron's dream too because literally the night before he agreed to his Nike contract, in the Nike contract there was this big... he got like a 20 or 30 percent bonus if he had gone to New York," Windhorst explained. "He literally agreed to that the night before the lottery."

Instead, the Cleveland Cavaliers landed the No. 1 pick in the lottery, and the rest is history. The 41-year-old played for multiple teams and enjoyed his trips to Madison Square Garden, but playing for New York was never in the cards.

Still, James admitted that joining the Knicks this offseason would have been on the table had they not won the 2026 NBA championship.

"He has always flirted with the idea of the Knicks for years," ESPN's Alan Hahn said (9:10 mark). "... I always felt like there was going to be a connection at some point. And that's what kind of makes me laugh now, like you were just saying, it's like now that it was finally time, the Knicks were like, 'No, we're good. We got what we needed. We won our championship, so we're all set.' Now, he flies a helicopter to New York instead."

James and the Sixers will open the 2026-27 season against the Knicks on Tuesday night at MSG, and he will have to watch their championship ring ceremony while wondering about what could have been.

articles.title: Bodiroga confirma que la Euroliga adoptará un sistema de dos conferencias el curso 2027-28
articles.standfirst: El torneo pasará de 20 a 24 equipos
articles.summary: El torneo pasará de 20 a 24 equipos
articles.body: El presidente de la Euroliga, Dejan Bodiroga, confirmó que la máxima competición continental cambiará su formato la temporada 2027-28, pasando de los 20 clubes actuales a 24 que se organizarán en dos conferencias. "El año que viene cambiaremos el formato: pasaremos de los 20 clubes actuales, en los que todos se enfrentan entre sí, a 24 equipos organizados en dos conferencias, aunque aún no hemos definido los criterios para la formación de las mismas", precisó Bodiroga en unas declaraciones al programa 'Radar Forum' recogidas por Mozzart Sport. Con el posible acuerdo con la NBA para organizar una competición conjunta muy lejos de cerrarse, la Euroliga sigue con su plan para los próximos años, que pasa por la expansión de las franquicias que se convertirán en miembros de pleno derecho de la organización. Actualmente, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Anadolu Efes, Baskonia, Fenerbahçe, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Olimpia Milán, Olympiacos, Panathinaikos, ASVEL, Bayern Munich, Zalgiris y CSKA Moscú son los 13 propietarios de la competición. En ese sentido, Bodiroga destacó que la Euroliga ha recibido "un interés considerable y numerosas ofertas", tanto de equipos que actualmente participan en la Eurocopa como de otros ajenos a ella, lo que demuestra una tendencia al alza constante de la competición que preside. "La Euroliga nunca ha sido tan fuerte como hoy. Estamos creciendo y avanzando conforme a nuestro plan estratégico. El año pasado, más de 3,3 millones de aficionados llenaron nuestros pabellones, mientras que más de 500 millones de espectadores siguieron nuestros partidos por televisión a lo largo de la temporada; la cifra más alta registrada hasta la fecha", precisó. Además, según Bodiroga, el torneo también ha experimentado un crecimiento significativo de interacción en las redes sociales y del número de patrocinadores: "Si observamos todos los indicadores, la Euroliga goza actualmente de un gran impulso".

articles.title: Joan Plaza sobre Sergio Llull y la NBA: "Hizo bien en no hacerme caso"
articles.standfirst: El exentrenador blanco repasa los inicios de Llull, su decisión de no dar el salto a la NBA y las claves para mejorar el baloncesto español
articles.summary: El exentrenador blanco repasa los inicios de Llull, su decisión de no dar el salto a la NBA y las claves para mejorar el baloncesto español
articles.body: Joan Plaza ha sido uno de los protagonistas de Marcador, en Radio MARCA, en una entrevista conducida por Álvaro Mongil y Carlos Santos con motivo de los 700 partidos de Sergio Llull en la Liga Endesa. El técnico, que dirigió al Real Madrid en los primeros pasos del base menorquín en el conjunto blanco, recordó cómo se gestó su llegada y qué le convenció de un jugador que acabaría convirtiéndose en una leyenda del club. "Era un jugador joven, era un jugador aguerrido, de la vieja escuela, de estos que, a pesar de que juegue para ganar dinero, juega para divertirse, juega para contagiar", explicó. Plaza reconoció que entonces nadie podía anticipar la dimensión que alcanzaría la carrera de Llull, aunque sí detectó desde el principio una cualidad diferencial: su capacidad competitiva y su facilidad para mejorar a quienes le rodeaban. "Yo creo que es una persona imprevisible ofensivamente", señaló el entrenador, que también quiso destacar su generosidad en el juego, su capacidad para repartir asistencias y su intensidad defensiva. Sobre su papel actual en el Real Madrid, fue contundente: "Él no va a bajar la guardia, es un competidor, es un ganador y va a saber esperar el momento". Uno de los momentos más destacados de la entrevista llegó al recordar la oferta de los Houston Rockets y las conversaciones que ambos mantuvieron sobre la posibilidad de cruzar el Atlántico. Plaza admitió que aconsejó a Llull aceptar el reto de la NBA, aunque el jugador terminó apostando por continuar en el Real Madrid y construir una trayectoria histórica. "Hizo bien en no hacerme caso a mí o a otros que le sugeríamos que viviera la experiencia en NBA", reconoció. Para el técnico, el deseo del menorquín de dejar huella en un club de la dimensión del conjunto blanco terminó pesando más que la aventura estadounidense. El exentrenador también reflexionó sobre la dificultad de encontrar jugadores que permanezcan durante tantos años en un mismo equipo y defendió la necesidad de cuidar el vínculo entre los clubes y sus referentes. En su opinión, la fidelidad no depende únicamente del jugador, sino también de que las entidades ofrezcan estabilidad, confianza y condiciones adecuadas para desarrollar una carrera a largo plazo. Llull, que ha sabido adaptarse a distintos roles y entrenadores, representa para Plaza un ejemplo de esa conexión entre rendimiento, compromiso y pertenencia. Por último, Plaza analizó la situación del baloncesto español y alertó de la necesidad de reforzar el trabajo de formación y favorecer la continuidad de los jugadores en la Liga Endesa. "Hay que trabajar mejor en categorías inferiores, hay que pagar mejor a esos entrenadores", defendió, al tiempo que reclamó competiciones atractivas y proyectos deportivos sólidos que permitan retener talento. El técnico insistió en que los aficionados necesitan reconocer a sus jugadores y crear vínculos duraderos con ellos. Una reflexión que, en una jornada marcada por los 700 partidos de Llull, cobra especial sentido al hablar de una carrera construida alrededor de un mismo escudo.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson Says 'There's No Relaxation' After Knicks Won 2026 NBA Title
articles.summary: The New York Knicks are just over 24 hours away from celebrating their first NBA championship since 1973, but team captain Jalen Brunson isn't letting his team take its foot off the gas.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are just over 24 hours away from celebrating their first NBA championship since 1973, but team captain Jalen Brunson isn't letting his team take its foot off the gas.

While speaking to reporters on Monday, Brunson was asked if winning the 2026 NBA championship would help him relax entering the 2026-27 campaign.

"There's no relaxation whatsoever," Brunson said bluntly.

Final Record Predictions for Every NBA Team 🔮

Brunson previously said it took him about a month to move on from celebrating the 2026 title win and begin focusing on winning a second straight championship ring.

The 2026 NBA Finals MVP, Brunson helped carry the Knicks to the mountaintop last season by defeating the San Antonio Spurs in five games. However, ESPN's Ben Golliver reported that 50 percent of the league's general managers voted for the Spurs to win the 2027 championship.

Brunson's mindset will help the Knicks avoid a championship hangover, but they will need to remain motivated throughout the year to navigate the competitive Eastern Conference.

The Knicks will hold their championship ring ceremony and open the season on Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden against the Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.body:
MADISON – The voters in the AVCA coaches poll are not quite as high on Wisconsin volleyball as the NCAA selection committee.

The Badgers are No. 6 in the Oct. 19 update to the coaches poll. That is the same as where they were in the previous week's coaches poll and two spots below where the NCAA selection committee slotted them in the in-season top 16.

The rankings follow a 2-0 week for UW with wins over unranked Maryland and Iowa – two teams that are a combined 3-13 in Big Ten matches. UW now has a 13-5 overall record, 7-1 Big Ten record and 8-5 record against ranked opponents.

Other ranked Big Ten teams include No. 1 Nebraska, No. 10 Oregon, No. 12 Purdue, No. 16 Penn State, No. 18 Indiana, No. 20 Minnesota and No. 21 Washington. Teams receiving votes include Michigan State, UCLA and Illinois.

The Badgers will face No. 21 Washington on Oct. 23 and unranked Michigan on Oct. 25 at the UW Field House.

articles.title: Lakers Waive Dalton Knecht in Latest NBA Rumors, Top Landing Spots for Former 1st-Round Draft Pick
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have parted ways with a former first-round draft pick.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have parted ways with a former first-round draft pick.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania, the team has waived Dalton Knecht, the No. 17 overall pick in 2024.

It's likely only a matter of time before the sharpshooter finds a new team. One potential landing spot for him could be the Charlotte Hornets, who attempted to trade for him during the 2024-25 season.

Knecht was a standout at Tennessee during the 2023-24 season, winning SEC Player of the Year while leading the Vols to an Elite Eight appearance. The Lakers picked him up in the first round in 2024, hoping he'd give them an offensive boost off the bench.

He averaged 9.1 points per game while shooting 37.6 percent from deep in 2024-25, and there were flashes of an elite offensive talent, like a 37-point performance against the Utah Jazz.

But after playing 19.2 minutes per game as a rookie, he played about half of that in Year 2 and appeared in 54 games. By the end of the season, he had fallen almost completely out of the rotation.

Knecht finished the 2025-26 campaign averaging 4.2 points per game.

While the Lakers didn't have much of a spot for Knecht, a handful of other teams would surely be willing to give the young player a chance.

It's fair to assume the Hornets will at least check in on him given their previous interest. Charlotte attempted to trade center Mark Williams to the Lakers in return for Knecht ahead of the trade deadline in 2025, but Williams didn't pass his physical, and the trade was rescinded .

The Hornets are a much different team now, with LaMelo Ball in Minnesota, but they could still use a sharpshooter like Knecht to come off the bench.

The Orlando Magic also jump out as a team in need of offensive depth after a dissapointing ending to last season. The team has one roster spot available heading into the year and could use it on Knecht.

articles.title: Hornets, Brandon Miller reportedly agree to $209M contract extension ahead of Monday's deadline
articles.summary: The two sides agreed to the deal Monday, hours ahead of a deadline for players from Miller's draft class to sign an extension.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets and Brandon Miller have agreed to a five-year, $209 million extension to his rookie contract, ESPN's Shams Charania reports — a deal cementing the No. 2 overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft as one of the cornerstones of the ongoing effort to build a consistent contender in the Queen City.

The two sides agreed to the deal Monday, hours ahead of a deadline for players from Miller's draft class to sign an extension. Had they not reached agreement on a deal, Miller would have played the upcoming season on a team option, then gone into next offseason as a restricted free agent.

Instead, Miller is under contract for five more seasons at $41.8 million per year after playing the first four seasons of his rookie contract for a total of $49.4 million.

The former Alabama standout bounced back from an injury-wracked sophomore season to turn in a stellar third campaign, averaging 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1 steal in 30.3 minutes per game with a career-best .574 true shooting percentage (which factors in 2-point, 3-point and free-throw accuracy). Miller was one of only a dozen wing players to hit those marks last season, according to Stathead ; 10 of the other 11 members of the list are All-Star and All-NBA honorees. (We see you, Trey Murphy III.)

The list of wings to produce like that by their age-23 season includes some of the brightest young perimeter players in the league in recent years — names like Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kevin Durant, James Harden, Jayson Tatum, Anthony Edwards, Devin Booker and Jalen Williams. That's the kind of company the Hornets are betting — and betting big — that Miller can continue to keep, developing into the kind of perennial All-Star and All-NBA candidate who can lift Charlotte into the ranks of the league's elite teams.

After missing most of the first month of the season following a left shoulder subluxation , Miller played a significant role in helping the Hornets climb out of an early hole to become one of the hottest teams in the NBA over the final few months. LaMelo Ball's high-octane playmaking and rookie Kon Knueppel's deadeye marksmanship drew the most headlines, but the 6-foot-7 Miller's all-around play on the wing — as a spot-up threat on the weak side of the primary action, as a complementary pick-and-roll ball-handler, as a speed demon sprinting the floor in transition, and as an improved multipositional perimeter defender — helped tie it all together for head coach Charles Lee's squad, which boasted the NBA's sixth-best record and second -best net rating after Christmas, according to Cleaning the Glass .

"Definitely [want to do] everything I can do to win a basketball game, whether that's guarding the best player, guarding a player that can't shoot or [has a] lower percentage, I take pride in that two-way mindset," Miller told Rod Boone of the Charlotte Observer last season . "It's been going great this year. We get a lot of wins when everybody's locked into that two-way mindset. So, just keep having that mindset."

That second-half surge led the Hornets to the verge of the postseason, with a play-in victory over the Miami Heat followed by a loss to the Orlando Magic in their second play-in contest. But despite coming within arm's reach of the franchise's first playoff appearance since 2016 , and despite playing the most exciting and energizing brand of ball that Hornets fans have seen in ages, Charlotte's brass elected to reorient the roster this summer, dealing Ball and guard Josh Green to the Minnesota Timberwolves in exchange for sweet-shooting forward Naz Reid, an unprotected 2033 first-round pick, swap rights on Minnesota's firsts in 2028, 2029 and 2030, and second-round picks in 2029, 2032 and 2033.

Whatever rationale you ascribe to the trade — the Hornets' front office not believing the roster was quite as good as that torrid second half suggested, seizing the opportunity to get out of the Ball business after he'd had a healthy season for the first time in four years, believing Coby White could replace most of Ball's production at a substantially lower dollar figure — it also represented, to some degree, a bet on Miller (and Knueppel) being able to expand his offensive game and shot-creation capabilities, and grow into the centerpiece of a winning organization, if given the opportunity.

"Brandon, I think everyone would agree he's an enormous talent," Hornets executive vice president of basketball operations Jeff Peterson told reporters this summer . "He showed a tremendous amount of growth last season battling through an injury, but was able to continue to persevere and again help us achieve some results that made our fan base and us very, very excited, proud. [...] Of course, everyone knows he's skilled and athletic, and he has a true desire to win and continue to get better. So could not be more excited to be going into next season with Brandon Miller on our squad."

To make the sort of impact that Peterson and the rest of Charlotte's braintrust believe he can, Miller will need to stay on the floor. He had surgery on that troublesome left shoulder after the season and spent the summer rehabilitating it, aiming to enter the 2026-27 campaign stronger, more stable and better able to take on the additional on- and off-court responsibilities awaiting him in Ball's absence, as one of the leaders on a team with its sights set on ending the NBA's longest ongoing postseason drought .

"Do I know if we are going to be good or great?" Miller said back in August . "I know we are going to be a hard-working team. It's not about who makes the most shots. It's about who can play consistently at 110% every night. I think that's one thing we are going to take pride in."

The Charlotte Hornets made Brandon Miller one of their presumed franchise cornerstones when they selected him with the No. 2 overall pick of the 2023 NBA draft, and they paid him accordingly on Monday.

The two sides agreed to a five-year, $209 million rookie contract extension, agents AJ Vaynerchuk and Joey Middleton told ESPN's Shams Charania.

NBA Stars with Most on the Line This Season 🫡

This comes after the Hornets exercised Miller's $15.1 million player option for the 2026-27 season in October 2025, which provided some stability in the immediate future but also put potential restricted free agency ahead of the 2027-28 campaign on the table.

That is no longer a concern following this development.

If nothing else, Charlotte got ahead of possible trade rumors that would have circulated with restricted free agency looming with this move. It also ensured one of its key young pieces will remain in place as it looks to build on a promising 2025-26 season.

The Hornets improved from a dreadful 19-63 record in 2024-25 to 44-38 in 2025-26 thanks to an impressive turnaround in the second half of the schedule. While it lost in the Eastern Conference play-in tournament, it provided a hint at what is to come for a team with plenty of young talent.

And Miller is a significant part of that young talent alongside Kon Knueppel, among others.

The Alabama product led the Hornets in scoring at 20.2 points per game in 2025-26, which was his third season in the league. He appeared in 65 games, which was an important step after injuries limited him to a mere 27 games in his second season in the league.

Miller also averaged 4.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.0 steals per game while shooting 43.5 percent from the field and 38.3 percent from deep. The efficiency stood out, as it marked a career-high in three-point shooting and a notable jump from the previous season when he shot 40.3 percent from the field.

He also dealt with a shoulder injury at times, suggesting he could be even better in the future if he remains healthy and picks up more experience.

After all, Miller is just 23 years old and has already established himself as one of the go-to options on an Eastern Conference team with a promising future that should be competing for playoff spots in the coming years.

If Miller lives up to expectations over the course of this new contract, the playoffs will be the baseline expectation in Charlotte.

articles.title: Kevin Porter Jr. Waived by Bucks in New NBA Rumors, Top Landing Spots for Guard
articles.summary: Kevin Porter Jr. had a career year in his first full season with the Milwaukee Bucks, but the team has decided to go in another direction ahead of the 2026-27 campaign.
articles.body:
Kevin Porter Jr. had a career year in his first full season with the Milwaukee Bucks, but the team has decided to go in another direction ahead of the 2026-27 campaign.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania, the Bucks have waived the guard.

NBA Stars with Most on the Line This Season 🫡

With Porter on his way out of Milwaukee, he'll look to join a new team before the season starts. One team in need of a guard could be the Sacramento Kings, who lost Ben Simmons to a season-ending torn Achilles on Sunday.

Porter, a first-round pick in 2019, started his career with the Cleveland Cavaliers before spending three seasons with the Houston Rockets. He started the 2024-25 season with the Los Angeles Clippers but was traded to the Bucks midway through the year.

Last year, Porter put up 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds and a career-high 7.4 assists in 38 games with Milwaukee. A lingering right knee injury forced him to miss the majority of the season.

Despite solid numbers last season, Porter struggled during the preseason, and the team ultimately decided to waive him to meet the roster limit.

Before being waived on Monday, Porter was drawing trade interest from the Kings, according to NBA insider Jake Fischer.

Now a free agent, Porter could join the Kings without Sacramento having to give up any assets in a trade. With Simmons out for the year, the Kings need some backcourt depth, and Porter makes for an intriguing offer.

Sacramento will surely use first-round pick Darius Acuff Jr. as its starting point guard, but Porter could play as his backup as the young player gets acclimated to the league.

The Minnesota Timberwolves added LaMelo Ball this offseason, but they don't have much depth behind him. Second-round pick Isaiah Evans is currently set to back up Ball, and Porter would be an upgrade.

Whether Sacramento, Minnesota or elsewhere, it's hard to imagine Porter will go unsigned for very long, especially as injuries start to take a toll on teams.

articles.title: Los sueños de la ÑBA
articles.standfirst: La FEB reúne a Hugo González, Aday Mara, Baba Miller y Sergio De Larrea, los españoles en la NBA junto a Santi Aldama, para hablar de la temporada que está a punto de comenzar
articles.summary: La FEB reúne a Hugo González, Aday Mara, Baba Miller y Sergio De Larrea, los españoles en la NBA junto a Santi Aldama, para hablar de la temporada que está a punto de comenzar
articles.body: La temporada NBA está a unas horas de arrancar con presencia de cinco jugadores españoles: Hugo González, Aday Mara, Baba Miller, Sergio De Larrea y Santi Aldama. Aprovechando una concentración de la selección española para unas Ventanas FIBA, la FEB reunió a los cuatro primeros para hablar en una divertida charla sobre el curso que está a punto de comenzar. Hugo González, el veterano, dio consejos a sus compañeros. "El año se hace largo. Son menos meses, pero la temporada es muy exigente. Estad concentrados toda la temporada. Hay altos y bajos, pero lo llevaréis bien. Os deseo la mejor de las suertes menos cuando juguéis contra los Celtics", dijo el alero antes de hablar de la vida fuera de la pista: "Es aburrida. No te da tiempo a mucho: comes, duermes, vuelves a entrenar, vuelves a viajar, no sabes dónde te levantas porque hay viajes muy largos con seis partidos fuera seguidos...". El jugador madrileño recomendó a los novatos que encontraran "una rutina que os ayude a activaros antes de los partidos y otra rutina para después de los partidos y hacer una correcta recuperación". De Larrea escuchó ese mismo consejo durante su paso por el Rookie Transition Program, un cursillo de varios días en el que los debutantes reciben instrucciones sobre cómo comportarse en la cancha y fuera de ella. Mara y Miller no acudieron este año, pero están obligados a hacerlo al próximo. Además de hablar sobre sus respectivas ciudades o los coches que van a tener, los cuatro hicieron una porra sobre cómo van a quedar sus equipos. Por supuesto, todos pusieron al suyo por encima de los demás. "2-0, 2-0 y 2-0", asegura Hugo sobre sus duelos contra los equipos de sus compañeros de selección. "Boston, Oklahoma, Clippers y Dallas", pronosticó para esta particular Liga con sabor español. La predicción de Baba fue: "Clippers, Dallas, Oklahoma y Boston". Mara visualiza "Oklahoma, Dallas, Boston y Clippers". Y 'Larry' acaba con "Dallas, Oklahoma, Boston y Clippers". A Mara le recordaron su poco prolífico paso por UCLA. Al hablar del pabellón de los Clippers, recordó que él había estado en un partido ante la Universidad de Gonzaga, aunque no llegó a saltar a la pista. "El destino me hizo pasar por eso para el siguiente año reventarla y callar bocas", dice el pívot sobre sus escasas oportunidades en la Universidad angelina y su posterior explosión en Míchigan. Para acabar, tratando de resumir su temporada en una sola palabra cuando finalice su curso, Mara elige "proceso"; Miller, "evolución"; De Larrea, "trabajo"; y Hugo, "ganar". Cuatro sueños españoles en la NBA. Y con Aldama, cinco. Un quinteto ÑBA.

articles.title: NBA Rosters for Lakers, Knicks, 76ers, All 30 Teams Unveiled Ahead of 2026 Opening Night
articles.summary: NBA fans have less than 24 hours to study the rosters for the new season.
articles.body:
NBA fans have less than 24 hours to study the rosters for the new season.

The league announced the full rosters for all 30 teams Monday ahead of Tuesday's season-opening tripleheader:

Some of the offseason's biggest additions will be on display from the opening day of the season, as the Boston Celtics will take on the Detroit Pistons before the Philadelphia 76ers face the reigning champion New York Knicks.

Philadelphia was under the spotlight throughout the offseason, as it added the legendary LeBron James and five-time All-Star Jaylen Brown. Brown arrived via a trade that sent Paul George to the Celtics, where he will play alongside Jayson Tatum and look to help lead the team on a deep playoff run.

As for the reigning champions, the Knicks roster won't look much different with Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart running things back. New York won its first championship since the 1972-73 campaign and has a number of players returning that know what it takes to reach the NBA's mountaintop.

If the Knicks do reach the Finals again, they could very well face one of the teams playing each other in the nightcap of Tuesday's tripleheader.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder in last season's Western Conference Finals and bring back much of the same core with Victor Wembanyama leading the way. As for the Thunder, they still have Shai Gilgeous-Alexander spearheading the group.

While the Spurs, Knicks and Thunder will have plenty of familiar faces, there are a number of headliners on new teams this season.

Most notably outside of the moves involving the 76ers and Celtics, Giannis Antetokounmpo is joining Bam Adebayo on the Miami Heat. The future Hall of Famer's presence will mean opposing defenses will have to pick their poison when facing Miami's frontcourt, which could set them both up for major seasons.

Elsewhere, Kawhi Leonard is returning to the Toronto Raptors franchise he led to the championship in 2019 and LaMelo Ball will be the point guard passing Anthony Edwards the ball this season.

It promises to be a thrilling 2026-27 campaign, and some of the league's most prominent names and teams will be in action right away during Tuesday's openers.

articles.title: Where Bronny James Fits on Lakers' Updated Depth Chart After Dalton Knecht Release
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers made the somewhat surprising decision to release former first-round pick Dalton Knecht on Monday, per ESPN's Shams Charania, leading to some interesting questions about the rotation heading into the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers made the somewhat surprising decision to release former first-round pick Dalton Knecht on Monday, per ESPN's Shams Charania , leading to some interesting questions about the rotation heading into the 2026-27 season.

Bronny, Luka and Reaves' Stats vs. Nuggets

Two notable players who made the roster over Knecht: Guards Bronny James and Jaden Hardy. Here's a look at how the depth chart could shake out:

PG: Luka Dončić; Collin Sexton; Bronny James

SG: Austin Reaves; Adou Thiero; Jaden Hardy

SF: Quentin Grimes; Matisse Thybulle; Cameron Carr

PF: Ziaire Williams; Jake LaRavia; Sandro Mamukelashvili; Jarred Vanderbilt

The reality is that James is unlikely to see significant minutes. Dončić, Reaves, Grimes and Sexton can all handle playmaking duties, and mixing and matching the team's various wing options will likely be a bigger priority than getting James much work in the rotation.

While James making the roster over Knecht may feel like a vote of confidence from head coach JJ Redick and the front office, it's just as likely that the Lakers felt Knecht was no longer a fit and needed a change of scenery.

"The team changed. The needs changed, the fit changed," Redick told reporters Friday regarding Knecht. "I think he got better as a player over the last two years. I think each guy has, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the amount of injuries we had. So I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings and he's in a tough spot right now."

The Lakers had a ton of turnover this offseason, reshaping the roster to better suit Dončić's skill set. But for all of the moving pieces, it's still hard to imagine a pathway—sans injuries—for Bronny to see many minutes.

articles.title: Kyrie Irving Hints at Early Retirement in New Comments, 'Not the Same NBA I Fell in Love With'
articles.summary: It doesn't seem like Dallas Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving is going to play in the NBA into his 40s.
articles.body:
It doesn't seem like Dallas Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving is going to play in the NBA into his 40s.

"Basketball is an eternal flame," the 34-year-old said Monday, per Christian Clark of The Athletic. "In terms of the NBA schedule and things of that nature, you have to really be in love with that, too. The weight lifting. The unseen hours. The media prep. Just going in and being ready to play at a high level. Also, you have social media and gambling right now, which is running rampant. It's not the same NBA I fell in love with as a kid."

He went on to say playing in the league has become "less human" and "more robotic" since he was the No. 1 overall pick of the 2011 NBA draft.

"I don't see myself playing in the NBA at 42, 43. Shoutout to the head honcho over there still going. Even Steph (Curry). Klay (Thompson) and James (Harden) and KD (Kevin Durant). I looked at those guys as big brothers for a while, but now that I'm in this age of 34, 35, I love my manhood and growing as a man more than growing as a basketball player."

The "head honcho" comment was likely a reference to LeBron James, who played alongside Irving on the Cleveland Cavaliers from the 2014-15 campaign through the 2016-17 one. They won a championship together, and James has since added another ring to his resume when he was with the Los Angeles Lakers.

James is now on the Philadelphia 76ers in what will be his age-42 season.

As for Irving, he missed the 2025-26 campaign as he recovered from a torn ACL that cut his previous season short after he appeared in 50 games.

He also hasn't reached the 70-game mark in a season since the 2016-17 one.

While he may not have that many seasons remaining in his career, Irving is one of the best guards of his generation with a resume that includes a championship, a Rookie of the Year, three All-NBA selections and nine All-Star nods.

Fans may want to make sure they see him in person this season because he is already thinking about retirement ahead of the Mavericks' opener on Wednesday against the Houston Rockets.

articles.title: Former Gator Walter Clayton Jr. waived by Memphis Grizzlies
articles.summary: The Memphis Grizzlies are waiving former Florida star Walter Clayton Jr. ahead of the NBA roster deadline, according to ESPN.
articles.body:
Walter Clayton Jr.'s second NBA season is taking an unexpected turn.

The Memphis Grizzlies are waiving the former Florida star along with forward Micah Peavy ahead of the NBA's roster deadline, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . The moves bring Memphis down to the league maximum of 15 players on standard contracts.

Clayton was the No. 18 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft and arrived in Memphis in February as part of the massive trade that sent Jaren Jackson Jr. to the Utah Jazz . He appeared in 24 games for the Grizzlies after the deal, averaging 9.7 points, 5.7 assists and 2.1 rebounds while shooting 36.6% from 3-point range.

His roster spot became less secure over the offseason. Clayton missed an important development window after suffering a knee injury during summer league. He struggled to build momentum in the preseason, shooting 33.3% from the field in 47 minutes across four games. Memphis also entered the season with considerable point guard depth.

Before waiving Clayton, Memphis reportedly explored the trade market for the second-year guard. CBS Sports and NBC Sports both reported Monday, citing NBA insider Marc Stein, that the Grizzlies were actively shopping Clayton before the roster deadline, with Sacramento emerging as a possible destination.

Clayton remains one of the most accomplished guards in Florida history after earning consensus All-America honors and Final Four Most Outstanding Player during the Gators' national championship run. He averaged 18.3 points and 5.7 assists in his final season in Gainesville.

He will now head to waivers, where another NBA team can claim his contract.

articles.title: ClutchPoints’ NBA MVP Mondays: Victor Wembanyama headlines list of 10 players to watch during 2026-27 season
articles.summary: The race for the 2026-27 NBA MVP award begins on Tuesday, and several featured stars will be in action on Opening Night. Not only will Jayson Tatum and Cade...
articles.body:
The race for the 2026-27 NBA MVP award begins on Tuesday, and several featured stars will be in action on Opening Night . Not only will Jayson Tatum and Cade Cunningham kick things off in the afternoon, but Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks will raise their championship banner against Tyrese Maxey and the Philadelphia 76ers.

Of course, then there is the final and third game of the night that everyone has been dying to see since last season's Western Conference Finals ended : the San Antonio Spurs and Victor Wembanyama against the Oklahoma City Thunder and two-time defending MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander .

That means six realistic MVP candidates will be playing to begin the 2026-27 season, setting the stage for what should be an incredible year-long race for the award.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Over the last few seasons, there hasn't been much change in the MVP voting.

Nikola Jokic has won the award three times since the start of the 2020-21 season, and if it wasn't for Joel Embiid in 2023, Jokic may have won the award four straight times. Many of the same names have either won the award or come close to doing so, as there have been four repeat winners over the last 12 seasons.

Gilgeous-Alexander is looking to make history, potentially joining the likes of Larry Bird, Wilt Chamberlain, and Bill Russell, by winning his third straight MVP award, but will voter fatigue catch up to the Thunder superstar?

Here are the top 10 of ClutchPoints' initial "MVP Mondays," which will be updated at the start of each week to reflect which players are standing out the most in the race for the 2026-27 NBA MVP award.

1. Victor Wembanyama – San Antonio Spurs

2025-26 season stats: 64 games, 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 3.1 blocks, 1.0 steals, 51.2 FG%, 34.9 3P%

Is anyone surprised to see Victor Wembanyama leading the pack in the MVP rankings entering the 2026-27 season? At this point, we might as well say that Wemby will be within the top three of the MVP rankings pretty much all season as long as he doesn't get hurt.

This was the case last season, and Wembanyama finished third in the MVP voting . The only reason he didn't win the award, outside of greatness from Gilgeous-Alexander and Jokic, is the fact that he did miss games and barely qualified for end-of-season honors like MVP.

If he had played in four, maybe five more games, the Spurs may have finished with a better record than the Thunder, which would've led to Wemby likely winning MVP. That is all a hypothetical game, though, and we'll truly never know the answer to this.

Heading into the 2026-27 season, Wembanyama has extra motivation after losing in the 2026 NBA Finals to the Knicks, and he's made it clear that his mission isn't to be the best in the world but to build off his success from the year prior that has made him the face of the NBA.

"I thought that's what it mean — DPOY means being the best defender on the planet. I got a lot of growth to do in that respect," Wembanyma said after the team's recent 123-103 preseason win over the Phoenix Suns. "I'm saying this because I got coaches who hold me to a very high standard, and now the standard isn't just being the very best on the planet. It's being better than last year."

Assuming Wembanyama takes another step forward as he did a season ago, he will be arguably the most efficient two-way player in the NBA. Media voters are always looking for the "new" name when it comes to the MVP and someone winning it back-to-back, which is why this could very well be Wemby's year.

2025-26 season stats: 64 games, 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds, 8.3 assists, 1.6 steals, 47.6 FG%, 36.6 3P%

The new-look Los Angeles Lakers revolve around Luka Doncic and what he will accomplish offensively alongside Austin Reaves. Honestly, the Lakers are only going to be a real title threat as long as Doncic is healthy, which puts him in prime MVP territory.

Last season, Doncic led the league in scoring for the second time in his career, and he finished fourth in the MVP voting as a result. With more scoring weapons around him this year and a key big man to run pick-and-roll sets with in Walker Kessler, Luka is gearing up to have his best season in a Lakers uniform.

Do not be shocked if Doncic leads the league in scoring yet again.

3. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander – Oklahoma City Thunder

2025-26 season stats: 68 games, 31.1 points, 4.3 rebounds, 6.6 assists, 1.4 steals, 55.3 FG%, 38.6 3P%

What more can Gilgeous-Alexander possibly do? That is what all of us are asking ahead of the 2026-27 season, as SGA will need to be even better than his last two historic seasons to possibly three-peat as MVP.

At 28 years old, the Thunder star is in the prime of his career and actually enters the new season with a chip on his shoulder. It is hard to believe Gilgeous-Alexander has something to prove, but last year didn't end the way Oklahoma City had hoped.

Fresh off their 2025 title run, the Thunder dealt with injuries all year and ultimately fell in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals to the Spurs, who also picked up four wins against the defending champions in the regular season.

Gilgeous-Alexander will be highly motivated to beat San Antonio during the regular season, and the goal for this young Thunder core is to regain their championship status. That is why Gilgeous-Alexander could very well hit a new level of historic averages and immediately leapfrog both Wemby and Doncic for the No. 1 spot in the MVP rankings as the season progresses.

2025-26 season stats: 65 games, 27.7 points, 12.9 rebounds, 10.7 assists, 1.4 steals, 56.9 FG%, 38.0 3P%

As long as he is healthy, Nikola Jokic will always be in the mix for the MVP award. More importantly for him, his "MVP clock" has reset in a way, since he hasn't won the award since the 2023-24 season, so he should have a better chance than the last two seasons.

The craziest thing about Jokic and the MVP award, other than the fact that he has won it three times in his career in four years, is that he has finished first or second in the voting for the award for six straight seasons. If that happens again during the 2026-27 season, Jokic will become the first player in NBA history to finish first or second in the MVP voting for seven straight years.

Jokic has also averaged a triple-double in back-to-back seasons. He could join Russell Westbrook as the only players in league history to average a triple-double in three straight years should he be able to do so again.

2025-26 season stats: 74 games, 26.0 points, 3.3 rebounds, 6.8 assists, 46.7 FG%, 36.9 3P%

Winning is all that matters to Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks. The 2026 Finals MVP is taking this mindset with him into the new season, as there is now a championship standard in Madison Square Garden.

Brunson will tell everyone he doesn't care about personal success and all of the accolades, but at the end of the day, every NBA player pays attention to what is being said about them and where they finish in certain award races.

Not only did the Knicks star fail to make the All-NBA First Team, but he didn't receive a single first-place, second-place, third-place, fourth-place, or fifth-place vote for MVP last year.

The Knicks' leader is one of the most humble leaders in the entire league who doesn't let his emotion get the best of him. But deep down inside, Brunson wants to win the MVP award really bad. He may even have all the slander and last year's MVP voting results on the wall in his room!

6. Anthony Edwards – Minnesota Timberwolves

2025-26 season stats: 61 games, 28.8 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.4 steals, 48.9 FG%, 39.9 3P%

Before he suffered his right knee injury and was forced to miss time near the end of the 2025-26 season, Anthony Edwards was constantly inside the top five of ClutchPoints' MVP rankings. Last year was Ant Man's best in the league, averaging career-highs in scoring and shooting efficiency.

Since he only played in 61 games, Edwards was ineligible for MVP and All-NBA status.

As he prepares for Year 7 with the Minnesota Timberwolves (which is hard to believe), Edwards is focused on finding ways to improve alongside All-Star guard LaMelo Ball. Now that Ball will be the primary playmaker at the point guard position, Edwards won't have all the pressure of making plays for others anymore.

This should only make Edwards a more lethal shooter and scorer since he will be fresher and ready to take advantage of mismatches late in games.

2025-26 season stats: 64 games, 23.9 points, 5.5 rebounds, 9.9 assists, 1.4 steals, 46.1 FG%, 34.2 3P%

What should we expect from the Detroit Pistons this upcoming year?

Fresh off their 60-22 season, the third best in franchise history, the Pistons enter the 2026-27 season with a slightly revamped roster around superstar guard Cade Cunningham. Isaiah Joe is an elite 3-point shooter with championship experience, and John Collins is a seasoned veteran who will provide extra athleticism and rebounding at the forward position.

If the Pistons can finish with the best record in what many are calling the best Eastern Conference ever, that will matter greatly in this year's MVP race. After all, the 25-year-old hasn't even hit the prime years of his career yet and just finished as an All-NBA First Team performer who also finished inside the top 5 of last year's MVP vote.

2025-26 season stats: 36 games, 27.6 points, 9.8 rebounds, 5.4 assists, 62.4 FG%, 33.3 3P%

When Giannis Antetokounmpo is healthy, he's heavily regarded as one of the five best players in the NBA. If you need any proof of this, just look at his seven straight All-NBA First Team selections before last year.

Now that Giannis is with the Miami Heat and coming off an injury-riddled year in Milwaukee, the two-time MVP has something to prove.

Antetokounmpo will do everything he can to make sure the Heat are title contenders, and if he remains healthy, he will assume his mantle as the best two-way forward in the NBA. Getting back to his 30-10-5 averages with the Heat shouldn't be a problem for the Greek Freak.

2025-26 season stats: 16 games, 21.8 points, 10.0 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 1.4 steals, 41.1 FG%, 32.9 3P%

This will be the first time in Jayson Tatum's career that he has not played with Jaylen Brown. Over the last nine years, Tatum and Brown have been synonymous with the Celtics' success, leading the team to a title in 2024.

The weight of the franchise now falls on Tatum's shoulders, meaning he will be the one who always has the ball in his hands late in games and will be making all the plays for others. Not to mention, the Celtics are arguably the best 3-point shooting team in the league, so Tatum will have the necessary help around him to help keep Boston near the top of the standings.

Tatum returned for 16 games last season after missing the vast majority of the year recovering from his torn Achilles. He is fully healed and ready to give it his all entering the 2026-27 season, which is why we can't write off the Celtics.

2025-26 season stats: 70 games, 28.3 points, 4.1 rebounds, 6.6 assists, 46.2 FG%, 36.7 3P%

LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, and Joel Embiid are the mega stars on the Philadelphia 76ers roster, but if this team is going to live up to the hype surrounding them, then it'll be Tyrese Maxey who takes the mantle as their No. 1 option and player.

Last season, Maxey led the 76ers as one of five players to average over 28 points per game, and he is turning 26 in November.

Between his dynamic ball-handling, playmaking abilities, and athleticism to change pace on offense, Maxey is the complete point guard who can tie James, Brown, and Embiid together to make this All-Star lineup work.

The 76ers have a chance to be a very special team this year, and if we know anything, it's that Maxey will not be the one sacrificing as a scorer and primary ball-handler for this team. That is what makes him a real MVP candidate.

articles.title: James Harden Without a Beard Trends Before 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: James Harden has rocked his signature beard from the moment he showed up in the NBA with the Oklahoma City Thunder. But every year or two, there’s a trending...
articles.body:
James Harden has rocked his signature beard from the moment he showed up in the NBA with the Oklahoma City Thunder.

But every year or two, there's a trending image that goes around of what Harden looks like without the thing that gave him his nickname, "The Beard."

Sometimes it's a very old picture of Harden, truly what he looked like before he got his beard.

Sometimes it's a look at some sort of altered or generated image. Now in the era of AI-generated pictures, it's easier than ever to imagine Harden without a beard, even if it can look a little bit fake.

On the eve of the 2026-27 NBA season, images have been circulating on social media of Harden without a beard. It has fans quite fired up.

One problem: They don't seem to be real.

There's nothing credible to suggest that Harden doesn't have his beard anymore.

There's just one image that doesn't look all that much like Harden that has managed to go viral like crazy in recent days on social media.

The image is going viral at accounts like this one:

If it doesn't display there, you can see it at this link .

There's one telling clue, though: The image appears to have originated with the account NBA Centel, which is a parody account that doesn't actually share real news but instead posts things for engagement and clout.

This post certainly worked out. It has gotten a ton of attention. It's just not true.

The fake post actually originated just a couple days after an official NBA social media account shared Harden's real feelings on his beard.

"Until I'm retired, I'm keeping the beard," Harden said in a video post:

Harden plays for the Cleveland Cavaliers now. He's been well-traveled since entering the NBA with the Thunder out of Arizona State.

But even more constant than his footwork in the lane, his ability to get to the foul line, his stepback 3-pointers and his great passing vision has been his beard.

Harden's teams hold promotions where they give out fake versions of his beard. There's only one guy known as "The Beard."

And the next time you see an image of supposedly Harden without his beard, know that it's not happening. He's keeping that beard on his face for as long as he's in the league.

articles.title: Lakers’ JJ Redick Makes Surprise Bronny James, Dalton Knecht Announcement
articles.summary: JJ Redick reveals unexpected news about Bronny James and Dalton Knecht as the Lakers approach a crucial roster decision. The post Lakers’ JJ Redick Makes Sur...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have an important roster decision to make Monday. Two players whose futures have drawn attention throughout the preseason were nowhere to be found at practice.

Bronny James and Dalton Knecht were excused from Monday's workout because they were feeling unwell, coach JJ Redick revealed ahead of Wednesday's regular-season opener against the Golden State Warriors.

"We had a couple of guys under the weather today — Bronny and DK were both excused absences," Redick told reporters.

The timing was particularly notable for Knecht, whose future remains uncertain as Los Angeles approaches the NBA's 2 p.m. Pacific roster deadline.

Redick confirmed that the Lakers would make their final roster decision before the deadline.

The team entered Monday with 16 guaranteed contracts, one more than the NBA's regular-season limit.

Although both players missed practice because of illness, their absences came after difficult preseason performances.

Dalton Knecht Faces Uncertain Future With Lakers

Knecht has emerged as a leading candidate to be moved as Los Angeles attempts to finalize its roster.

According to NBA insider Marc Stein of The Stein Line , the Lakers spent the weekend exploring a workable trade involving the former first-round pick, potentially in exchange for another big man.

NBA insider Jake Fischer previously reported that Los Angeles discussed a deal with the Milwaukee Bucks involving center Jericho Sims , although there was skepticism about whether an agreement could be reached.

Knecht's struggles have hardly helped his situation.

The 25-year-old averaged just 2.8 points across four preseason appearances, shooting 25% from the field.

He scored 11 points against Golden State on Oct. 6 but went scoreless in his other three appearances, including the Lakers' final two exhibition games.

Knecht also averaged only 4.2 points in 54 regular-season games last season after showing promise during his rookie campaign.

Redick recently acknowledged that the Lakers' roster needs have changed, complicating Knecht's path toward playing time.

"The team changed. The needs changed, the fit changed," Redick said before Friday's preseason finale . "I think he got better as a player over the last two years. I think each guy has, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the amount of injuries we had. So I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings and he's in a tough spot right now."

With Quentin Grimes , Matisse Thybulle and other perimeter options now available, Knecht faces considerably more competition.

His absence Monday was attributed to illness, not a pending transaction.

Bronny James Also Misses Practice After Rough Preseason

James' absence came after an equally challenging preseason.

The 22-year-old guard averaged 2.2 points, 2.8 assists and 2.4 rebounds in five appearances while shooting 25% from the field.

His final two outings were particularly difficult.

James went scoreless against Golden State on Oct. 13, committing four turnovers in 11 minutes. He also failed to score in 12 minutes against Denver in Friday's preseason finale.

Redick had already expressed disappointment with James' preseason performances while acknowledging that his practices had been more encouraging.

"I don't think he's played well," Redick said after the Lakers' second preseason loss to Golden State.

James, however, is not facing the same level of reported trade speculation as Knecht.

The Lakers exercised his contract option during the offseason, signaling their continued interest in his development following LeBron James ' departure.

Monday's absence does not necessarily threaten his availability Wednesday.

Elsewhere, Collin Sexton returned to full practice after missing the entire preseason, while Adou Thiero and Cameron Carr remained limited .

But the Lakers' immediate concern is their roster deadline.

And until the front office makes its decision, Knecht's future remains the biggest unanswered question.

articles.title: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama Turns Heads With Latest Comments on Thunder’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder have developed one of the NBA’s most intriguing rivalries, with Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander...
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder have developed one of the NBA's most intriguing rivalries, with Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander emerging as two of the league's biggest superstars.

However, despite the competitive nature of their relationship, Wembanyama recently offered some revealing comments about the Thunder's franchise player that might surprise fans who believe there is genuine animosity between the two.

Speaking with reporters, Wembanyama expressed admiration for Gilgeous-Alexander and the consistency required to remain among the NBA's elite. His remarks, shared by Spurs reporter Matt Guzman, provided an interesting perspective on how the San Antonio superstar views his Oklahoma City counterpart.

Rather than dismissing his rival, Wembanyama acknowledged just how difficult it is to sustain greatness throughout an NBA career.

Victor Wembanyama Shares Honest Thoughts About Thunder's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander

"It's so impressive. It's so impressive because I'm now seeing firsthand what it feels like, what it looks like to play intentionally. To play in the Finals. To play nine-plus months of NBA basketball," Wembanyama said.

The Spurs star continued by questioning how players such as Gilgeous-Alexander, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Nikola Jokić manage to maintain their excellence over extended careers.

"And I wonder how these guys do it for 10, 15 years … it's the most impressive thing about great NBA players."

Those comments carry particular significance considering the growing rivalry between San Antonio and Oklahoma City. Wembanyama and Gilgeous-Alexander are two of the NBA's most recognizable talents, and their respective franchises have championship aspirations.

Naturally, that competition has created passionate discussions among both fan bases about which superstar deserves greater recognition. However, Wembanyama's latest remarks demonstrate that competing against another superstar doesn't necessarily prevent a player from appreciating his accomplishments.

Spurs and Thunder Rivalry Comes With Mutual Respect

Gilgeous-Alexander has established himself as one of basketball's premier offensive players, combining remarkable consistency with an ability to control games through his scoring and decision-making.

Wembanyama, meanwhile, brings a completely different skill set, using his extraordinary size, defensive instincts and expanding offensive arsenal to influence games.

Their contrasting styles make the Spurs-Thunder matchup particularly compelling, especially as both franchises look toward sustained championship contention. Still, Wembanyama's comments suggest he understands something that can occasionally get lost in debates surrounding NBA rivalries.

Being talented enough to compete with the league's best players is one accomplishment. Maintaining that standard year after year is another challenge entirely. For Wembanyama, Gilgeous-Alexander represents one of the players who have demonstrated what sustained excellence looks like.

And while the Spurs superstar undoubtedly wants to surpass Oklahoma City's franchise centerpiece on the court, his latest comments make one thing clear. Respect and rivalry can exist at the same time.
